            How are ratings calculated?
            To calculate the overall star rating and percentage breakdown by star, we don’t use a simple average. Instead, our system considers things like how recent a review is and if the reviewer bought the item on Amazon. It also analyses reviews to verify trustworthiness.

            Customers find the phone to be a premium device with top-notch camera quality, particularly praising its 50MP main camera with OIS and smooth 120Hz refresh rate display.               The Samsung Galaxy M36 5G is a strong mid-range phone that balances performance, display quality, and long-term value. It features a 6.7-inch Super AMOLED display with a smooth 120Hz refresh rate, delivering sharp and vibrant visuals.

              Powered by the Exynos 1380 processor, it handles daily tasks and multitasking with ease. The 50MP main camera with OIS captures crisp, stable photos even in low light, while the 5,000mAh battery ensures all-day power.

              Samsung also promises up to six years of software updates, which is a huge plus for longevity. On the downside, it lacks a headphone jack and uses a teardrop notch, which feels a bit dated in design.

              ⭐ Rating: 4.4/5

              Pros: Smooth display, strong performance, long updates, good camera, Feels good in hands.

              Cons: No headphone jack, older-style notch.

              Verdict: A dependable and future-ready 5G phone with Samsung’s trusted quality — perfect for users seeking performance and durability at a fair priing.

              this is the worst product of the Samsung that Amazon sells , on first day the phone was not working well ( Swipe UP issue , Lagging , Hanging , Battery charging and draining issues ) and I contacted Amazon and Samsung , Amazon suggested to obtain DOA letter from Samsung .During my interaction with Samsung customer support representatives, I was advised to visit the service center with the intention of submitting my device for required letter not for repair. However, I made it explicitly clear that I was not willing to proceed with a repair, as I do not wish to retain a faulty device under any circumstances.

              From the beginning, my consistent and firm request has been for a DOA (Dead on Arrival) certificate or a denial letter, which would enable me to proceed with a replacement through appropriate channels. I am highly disappointed that despite my clear communication, the process was directed toward repair, contrary to my consent and preference.

              I strongly object to this approach. It is both unfair and unreasonable to push a customer toward a repair process when the device is evidently defective, especially when the customer has categorically requested documentation for a replacement. My time and trust as a consumer are being taken for granted, and this experience is completely out of alignment with the standards expected from a brand of Samsung’s stature.
